paragraphs: §Stephen, Full of the Holy Spirit
Then the Chief Priest said, "What do you have to say for yourself?"

Stephen answered, "Friends, fathers, brothers — hear me out. The glorious God appeared to our ancestor Abraham back when he was living in Mesopotamia, before he ever moved to Haran. God told him, 'Leave your country and your family behind, and go to the land I will show you.'"

"So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and settled in Haran. After his father died, God moved him to this very country where you're living now. But God didn't give him any of it — not even a tiny plot to stand on. He did promise, though, to give the land to Abraham and his descendants later, even though Abraham didn't have a single child yet. God also warned him: his descendants would live as foreigners in another country, enslaved and brutalized for four hundred years. 'But,' God said, 'I will step in and deal with those slave masters, and bring my people out so they can worship me right here.'"

"Then God made a covenant with Abraham and sealed it on Abraham's body through circumcision. When Isaac was born, Abraham circumcised him eight days later. Isaac became the father of Jacob, and Jacob the father of the twelve patriarchs — and each of them faithfully passed the covenant sign down."

"But those patriarchs got jealous and sold their brother Joseph as a slave to Egypt. God stuck with Joseph, though. He rescued him from every trouble and got him noticed by Pharaoh, the king of Egypt. Pharaoh was so impressed that he put Joseph in charge of the entire country — even his own household."

"Then a famine hit the whole region, from Egypt all the way to Canaan, and things got desperate. Our ancestors were starving with no food in sight. Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt and sent our fathers to check it out. They confirmed it and went back a second time to buy food. That's when Joseph told his brothers who he really was and introduced the whole Jacob family to Pharaoh. Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and the rest of the family — seventy-five people in all. That's how the Jacob family ended up in Egypt."
"Jacob died there, and our ancestors after him. Their bodies were taken to Shechem and buried in the tomb Abraham had bought for a good price from the sons of Hamor."

"As the four hundred years were nearly up — the time God had promised Abraham for rescue — our people in Egypt had grown huge in number. But now Egypt had a king who had never even heard of Joseph. He crushed our people ruthlessly — he even forced us to abandon our newborn babies, leaving them out in the open to die a cruel death."

"Right in the middle of all that, Moses was born — a beautiful, beautiful baby. His family hid him at home for three months. When they couldn't hide him any longer, they put him outside — and Pharaoh's daughter found him immediately and raised him as her own son. Moses got the best education Egypt had to offer, and he grew up impressive both as a thinker and as an athlete."

"At forty, Moses got curious about how his fellow Hebrews were doing, so he went to see for himself. He caught an Egyptian beating one of them, so he stepped in and floored the Egyptian to avenge his oppressed brother. He figured his brothers would be thrilled he was on their side — that they'd see him as God's chosen deliverer. They didn't see it that way at all. The next day he saw two of them fighting and tried to break it up: 'Come on, shake hands. Friends, you're brothers — why are you beating each other up?'"

"The one who'd started the fight shot back, 'Who made you our boss? Are you going to kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?' When Moses heard that, he knew the word was out — so he ran for his life and lived as an exile in Midian. During those exile years, he had two sons."

"Forty years later, out in the wilderness near Mount Sinai, an angel appeared to him looking like flames in a burning bush. Moses couldn't believe his eyes, so he went closer to check it out. Then he heard God's voice: 'I am the God of your fathers — the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Moses was terrified out of his mind; he shut his eyes and turned away."

"God said, 'Kneel and pray. You're standing on holy ground — a holy place. I've seen how my people are suffering in Egypt. I've heard their groans. I've come down to help them. So get ready — I'm sending you back to Egypt.'"

"This is the same Moses they had rejected earlier, saying, 'Who put you in charge of us?' This is the Moses God sent back as ruler and rescuer — using that angel blazing in the burning bush. He led them out of slavery. He did amazing things, setting up God-signs all over Egypt, at the Red Sea, and out in the desert for forty years. This is the Moses who told the people, 'God will raise up a prophet just like me from among your own people.' This is the Moses who stood between the angel speaking on Sinai and our ancestors gathered in the desert — he took the life-giving words God gave him and handed them to us. Words our ancestors wanted nothing to do with."

"They missed the good old days in Egypt and whined to Aaron, 'Make us gods we can see and follow! This Moses who dragged us out here into the middle of nowhere — who knows what happened to him!' So they made a calf idol, offered sacrifices to it, and threw themselves a party to celebrate their brand-new religion."

"God was not pleased — not at all. But he let them have it their way: go ahead, worship every shiny new god that comes along, and live with the consequences. The prophet Amos spelled out those consequences: 'Did you bring me animal and grain offerings during those forty years in the desert, Israel? Hardly. You were too busy building shrines to war gods and sex goddesses, worshiping them with everything you had. That's why I sent you into exile in Babylon.'"

"And through all of that, our ancestors carried a tent-shrine for worshiping the true God, built to the exact blueprint God gave Moses. They took it with them when they followed Joshua into the land God cleared of pagans, and they kept it all the way down to David's time. David asked God for a permanent place of worship — but it was Solomon who built it."

"But that doesn't mean the Most High God actually lives in a building made by human carpenters and masons. The prophet Isaiah nailed it: 'Heaven is my throne room; I rest my feet on the earth. So what kind of house are you going to build me?' says God. 'Some place where I can get away and relax? It's already built — and I built it myself.'"

"And you are just as stubborn! Your hearts are calloused, your ears are shut! You keep deliberately ignoring the Holy Spirit — you're exactly like your ancestors. Name one prophet they didn't treat this way. Your ancestors killed anyone who dared to announce the coming of the Just One. And you've carried on the family business — traitors and murderers, every one of you. You received God's Law hand-delivered by angels — gift-wrapped! — and you threw it away!"

At that, they lost it completely — a screaming mob of catcalls, whistles, and insults. But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, barely noticed. His eyes were locked on God, whom he saw in all his glory, with Jesus standing at his side. He cried out, "Look! I see heaven wide open, and the Son of Man standing at God's side!"

Yelling and hissing, the mob drowned him out. Then, in a full stampede, they dragged him out of the city and started pelting him with rocks. The ringleaders took off their coats and left them with a young man named Saul to watch.

As the rocks rained down, Stephen prayed, "Master Jesus, receive my life." Then he dropped to his knees and prayed loud enough for everyone to hear, "Master, don't hold this sin against them." Those were his last words. Then he died. And Saul was right there, congratulating the killers.
